title: To Build a Fire
author: Jack London (1908)
low: comfortable and satisfying sleep he had ever known

threads.label: The old-timer's warning
threads.plant: The old-timer on Sulphur Creek had told him about it the previous fall
threads.payoff: You were right, old hoss; you were right

threads.label: The dog's instinct
threads.plant: It knew that it was no time for travelling
threads.payoff: trotted up the trail in the direction of the camp it knew

note: Hand labels by Claude (sandhi session, 2026-10-04): one editorial reading, kept small. Two turn quotes: the fall through the ice that wets his feet, and the snow that blots out the fire (the reversal). 7,081 words: past Gemini Nano's one-call window, so the page reads it in parts.
